claims.text: Local short-range chemical fluctuations govern the structural and chemical stability of high-entropy nanoalloys at high temperature.
Short-range chemical fluctuations govern stability by mediating thermo-plastic instabilities.
Compressive stress drives the microstructure from a clustered state toward a more ordered state.
The compression-induced ordered state better resists subsequent deformation.
Al0.1CrCoFeNi has inherent chemical clustering in its initial state.
The initial Al0.1CrCoFeNi material is a nominal random solid solution.
Thermo-plastic instabilities become significant at approximately 600–900 K.
AlxCrCoFeNi exhibits substantial chemical clustering over a wide temperature range when x is below 0.5.
At elevated temperature, thermal energy activates atomic rearrangements in the alloy.
High-strain compression promotes atomistic rearrangements in Al0.1CrCoFeNi at various temperatures.
Compression-facilitated atomic rearrangements produce a clustering-to-ordering transition.
The clustering-to-ordering transition stabilizes the structure by reducing fluctuations responsible for thermo-plastic instability.
The clustering-to-ordering transition is less pronounced or absent under tensile loading.
Compression at high temperature will increase local chemical ordering relative to tensile or unloaded conditions.
Increased local chemical ordering can be observed through pair-distribution-function changes or diffraction-peak sharpening.
Compressively loaded samples will resist further stress-induced structural fluctuations better than tensile or unloaded samples.
The proposed behavior is limited to compositions near Al0.1CrCoFeNi and regimes with sufficient atomic mobility but without wholesale phase transformation or melting.
